writer.headline: AI Money, Guardrails, and Power Limits

tldr.text: AI funding stayed hot, while bigger firms bought more AI tools.
Governments and courts tightened AI and voter-roll rules.
Power limits and oil shocks kept pressure on costs.

intro.text: The biggest shift was in AI Money Shift: money kept rushing into AI, from startups to big acquisitions. Governance Guardrails and The Power Limit also heated up, as trust, rules, and electricity became harder to ignore.

threads.line: AI Money Shift heated up because investors kept backing AI startups and big buyers kept spending on AI capabilities.
Governance Guardrails heated up as AI labs and institutions added stricter controls, disclosures, and policy framing.
The Power Limit heated up because AI needs more electricity, while supply and siting pressures made expansion harder.
Fragmented Israel stayed hot as the vote looked split, which points to longer coalition talks.
Refinery Shock heated up because fresh oil supply scares kept pushing prices up and feeding inflation worries.
Regulation vs Press heated up as courts, media, and industry pushed back on new rules.
Roll Trim heated up because voter-roll deletions and new paperwork drew wider public resistance.

writer.watch: Watch whether AI spending keeps broadening beyond startups into infrastructure and regulated industries. Also watch whether power and oil costs start slowing that expansion, and whether India’s rule changes trigger more legal pushback.
